Legal cigarette sales jump 55 per cent in Queensland after black market crackdown
Legal cigarette sales rose sharply in Queensland after the state gained stronger powers to shut illegal shops, while the national market remained largely flat at the same time.

The state's sales rose 55 per cent in the first month after new enforcement laws took effect in November and remained 40 to 45 per cent above previous levels for the following six months, according to data from major supermarkets and other retailers provided to the Illicit Tobacco and E-cigarette Commissioner.
Calls to Quitline also more than doubled in the 10 days following major enforcement operations, which suggested the crackdown may be encouraging some smokers to quit.

Hill says 'false thesis' being pushed about government spending
Assistant Minister Julian Hill says a "false thesis" is being pushed by some about the federal government's level of spending.
The federal government's Final Budget Outcome showed government spending was revised up since May's budget to 26.9 per cent of GDP.
Yesterday on Insiders, Treasurer Jim Chalmers flagged savings measures in upcoming Mid-Year Economic and Fiscal Outlook (MYEFO).
The assistant minister defended the government's current savings measures and has blamed the war in the Middle East of rising costs.
Speaking to ABC News Breakfast earlier, Hill says rising fuel prices are "cascading" through the economy.

"We can't accept this frankly false thesis being pushed by some parts of the political spectrum, simple solutions to complex global issues that somehow it's all a spending issue. It's simply not the truth of it," Hill says."The war in Middle East is the biggest single determinant in the price of fuel which we then as we know cascades through the economy."

Tehan labels pre-COP Pacific meeting a 'farce'
Shadow Energy Minister Dan Tehan says the pre-COP meeting in the Pacific organised by Australia isn't good value for money for taxpayers.
The climate change minister has refused to outline the cost of organising the UN meeting ahead of the main event next month.
Tehan has labelled the event a "farce" and has accused the prime minister of leaving the country during a cost-of-living crisis.
The Coalition dropped its policy of reaching net zero emissions by 2050 under former Liberal leader Sussan Ley.
So does Tehan think rolling back climate laws will lose Australia's standing with the Pacific at a time Australia is competing with China?
The shadow minister tells ABC Radio National Breakfast Australia has "serious" domestic challenges that need to be addressed.
"I do think that we're much better off if we're helping the Pacific with a strong economy where we are making sure that we're looking after Australians," Tehan says.
Key Event
Bowen refuses to outline cost of pre-COP meeting in Pacific
Climate Change Minister Chris Bowen has refused to outline the total cost of organising the pre-COP meeting in Fiji and Tuvalu.
PM Anthony Albanese and Bowen are attending the multi-day UN event ahead of next month's main conference.
Australia won a commitment to hold the event with Pacific nations as part of its agreement with Türkiye.
But the event has come under the spotlight after the federal government struggled to attract prime ministers and presidents.
Asked on ABC Radio National Breakfast what the event cost Australian taxpayers, Bowen sidestepped the question.
Pressed on whether the event's cost was $20 million, Bowen says that number is "keeping with estimates".

"This is the most important diplomatic engagement Australia will have in the Pacific this term. This is the most important climate conference that's been held in the Pacific, probably ever, at least in a decade," Bowen says."If you care about the Pacific, if you care about our region, and you care about Australia's influence in our region, then you support this process."

"This is the most important diplomatic engagement Australia will have in the Pacific this term. This is the most important climate conference that's been held in the Pacific, probably ever, at least in a decade," Bowen says.
"If you care about the Pacific, if you care about our region, and you care about Australia's influence in our region, then you support this process."
Assistant minister highlights figures showing rise in legal tobacco sales
Assistant Minister Julian Hill has seized on figures showing legal tobacco sales rose 55 per cent in Queensland following stronger enforcement.
The state's sales rose 55 per cent in the first month after new enforcement laws took effect in November and remained 40 to 45 per cent above previous levels for the following six months.
Federal Labor has been under pressure to reduce the tobacco excise after the Coalition and One Nation pledged to drastically reduce the tax.
Speaking to ABC Radio National Breakfast, Hill says strong licensing laws, tougher penalties, long-term closure orders and landlord penalties are effective in tackling illicit tobacco.
"We're not in some race to the bottom or bidding war with organised crime. That's not the government's policy. We're not going to surrender our health policy to these people," Hill says.
"Imagine a world where you wiped out all tobacco excise, the illegal cigarettes are still cheaper. You still have to go after the crooks and shut the shop and disrupt the criminal syndicates."
Joyce points to China's construction of coal-fired power stations
One Nation MP Barnaby Joyce says his party would use taxpayer money to build new coal-fired power stations in Australia.
Speaking to Channel Seven, Joyce has pointed to China as an example for building new coal-fired power stations.
"You'd have to look at what they're doing in China. They just roll them basically off the plans," Joyce says.
"If you go to build something that's first of type, you're going to pay a lot more money than if you build something that's more affordable."
But Labor MP Josh Burns has called the plan "mad" and has accused Joyce of wearing a "tinfoil hat".

"Our productivity of Australia is something that's so important, right? We need to make sure we're producing more. And the idea that we would go back and take away all of the science-based renewable energy projects is just mad," Burns says.
Key Event
Pre-COP kicks off today in Fiji
Bula from warm and humid Fiji 🌴🍹
Pre-COP is kicking off today and I'll be your eyes and ears on the ground, bringing you everything you need to know over the coming days.
Pre-COP is a multi-day United Nations event featuring high-level climate talks, ahead of next month's main conference.
You might recall that Australia handed hosting rights for COP31 to Türkiye in exchange for Bowen becoming President of Negotiations.
The deal also meant a lead-up event would be held in Fiji and Tuvalu, which is why we're here.
